title: indigo_test: wait for removed scheduler tasks to leave the task list instead of checking once
description: Found 2026-11-25 (scheduler integration suite, 1 of 5 runs failed). test_agent_scheduler.c:1287 ASSERT_FALSE(task_label("Aborted", ...)) runs immediately after the message "Task 'Aborted' aborted and deleted". The agent sends that message in finish_stop() (indigo_agent_scheduler.c ~1535) before remove_task(), and AGENT_SCHEDULER_TASK_STATE is republished on a later pass, so the test can still see the old entry. Fix the test: wait (bounded, e.g. 5 s) until the entry is gone instead of checking once; check the other single-shot ASSERT_FALSE(task_label(...)) checks that follow a message (lines ~1062-1065, 1208, 1436-1437, 1461, 2504, 2514, 2542) for the same race and convert those that are exposed. Test-only change, no agent behaviour change.

outcome.summary:
Race analysis is right for all five converted checks: delete_task (indigo_agent_scheduler.c:3052-3073) and delete_all_tasks (3145-3168) reply before the list is rebuilt, finish_stop sends "aborted and deleted" (1535) before remove_task, and AGENT_SCHEDULER_TASK_STATE is only republished by refresh() in the process pass (2921) or at task start (1648). Unconverted checks are safe: Broken/Nameless/Pending/Urgent hook never exist in any list; Other/Pending (test 2555-2556) are removed in the same DELETE_ALL list as Long; 2569 follows a restart where Other cannot exist. Formatting, 5 s timeout and failure diagnostic match wait_task_state; git diff --check passes. Evidence (1/5 full-suite failure, code-order cause, 0/40 in isolation) is adequate for a test-timing fix.

Defect (must fix): wait_task_gone (test_agent_scheduler.c:257-267) treats a missing AGENT_SCHEDULER_TASK_STATE as "gone". update_task_state_property (agent 993-1006) republishes a changed list as indigo_delete_property followed by indigo_define_property, and the bus calls the observer synchronously (indigo_bus.c:1370-1393), so for a short window the deleted() callback (test 123-135) leaves the cached property NULL and task_label returns false. If a poll lands in that window: (a) the helper returns true early, and the single-shot positive checks right after it fail: task_label("Long") at 1222, task_label("Hook only")/task_count()==1 at 2517-2518 (task_count returns -1), Prepare/Park/Morning/task_count()==3 at 2557-2560; (b) the assertion is weakened: a task that never disappears but whose label changes (any redefine) can still be reported as gone. The window is small but widens when the agent thread is preempted under the parallel full-suite load this ticket targets. Fix: take one snapshot per poll and return true only when the property is present and has no item for the name (e.g. inline the scan, or have the helper check property != NULL before scanning); keep failing after the timeout otherwise.

Out of s

Round 2: pass. Round-1 fix verified: wait_task_gone() (test_agent_scheduler.c:256-280) takes one snapshot per poll and returns true only for a defined AGENT_SCHEDULER_TASK_STATE without a "<name> | " item, so the delete/define gap of update_task_state_property (indigo_agent_scheduler.c:983) cannot end the wait early; the prefix match and timeout diagnostics mirror task_label/wait_task_state. Race analysis: all five converted checks (Gamma :1091 after DELETE_TASK, Flash :1234 after the Starting message, Aborted :1312 after the delete message, Work :2529 and Long :2567 after DELETE_ALL) follow a reply or message sent before refresh() republishes the list; each task was in the list beforehand, so no vacuous pass. Unconverted negatives are safe: Broken/Nameless :1461-1462, Pending :1486 and Urgent hook :2539 never enter the list; Other/Pending :2568-2569 were listed (TOTAL 6 waited) and delete_all_tasks removes all non-hook tasks in one pass with a single later republish, so the defined list without Long already lacks them, and a later redefine gap only makes a negative check pass correctly; Other :2582 follows task_count()==3 after restart. Alpha :1088 depends on the out-of-scope Gamma positive check (owner informed). No assertion weakened: each ASSERT_FALSE became an ASSERT_TRUE on a stricter bounded condition; removed unused label in abort_and_delete_running_task. Formatting: tabs, braces, one-line calls; git diff --check clean. No findings.

history.text: Building and running the affected integration cases

Reproduction: 1 failure of abort_and_delete_running_task in 5 full-suite runs on master (2026-11-25, run 5: test_agent_scheduler.c:1287 still saw the entry after 'aborted and deleted'). Not reproducible in isolation: 0/40 for both master and the fix under 6 busy loops on 4 cores. Cause from code order: the agent sends the message (finish_stop) or acknowledges DELETE_TASK / DELETE_ALL before AGENT_SCHEDULER_TASK_STATE is republished on a later pass (refresh). Fix: new bounded helper wait_task_gone(name, 5 s) at the five exposed single-shot checks (Gamma after DELETE_TASK, Flash after the message of Long, Aborted after the delete message, Work and Long after DELETE_ALL). The checks for tasks that never appear (Broken, Nameless, Pending, Urgent hook) and Alpha (checked after a positive wait on the same list) are not exposed and were left. Results: affected cases pass; full integration suite 173/173; flow check whitespace passed (unit is not selected for this file).
Implementation resumed: the review requested changes

Review round 1 fix: wait_task_gone() treated a missing AGENT_SCHEDULER_TASK_STATE as 'gone'; the agent deletes and redefines that property when labels change (update_task_state_property), so a poll in that gap returned early. It now takes one snapshot per poll and returns true only when the property is defined and has no item for the task. Correction to the earlier note: Alpha (line ~1075) follows a single-shot positive check of Gamma after a rename (line ~1074), not a positive wait; edit_task/replace_text do not refresh the list, so the Gamma check has the same race in the positive direction. Not changed here (outside the ticket's ASSERT_FALSE scope); reported to the owner.
